artifacts.name: About this indicator
artifacts.summary: Maps and counts genuinely private, residential swimming pools across the area. Their density is a lens on individual heat-adaptation capacity — who can cool down at home — and, set against public cool locations, on a climate-justice dimension of heat resilience.
artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Private pools explorer

artifacts.description:
The true OpenStreetMap geometry of every counted feature — points, ways and areas — carrying its name and (where mapped) opening hours. It appears from a neighbourhood zoom level so you can inspect the individual objects rather than an aggregate.

artifacts.name: Private pools over time
artifacts.summary: How the number of mapped private pools changed over time (+178% since 2016). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The count of private pools in the area at successive dates, reconstructed from OpenStreetMap history via the ohsome API. A rising line can reflect real-world growth **or** improving OpenStreetMap coverage — read it alongside the data-quality note.

artifacts.name: Density distribution
artifacts.summary: How private pools density varies across neighbourhoods, as a Lorenz curve (Gini 0.75; 0 = perfectly even, 1 = all in one sub-area). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The distribution of private pools density (per km²) across the area’s administrative sub-areas, shown as a Lorenz curve (Gini 0.75; 0 = perfectly even, 1 = all in one sub-area). A long tail or low median points to many under-served neighbourhoods.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Statistics
artifacts.summary: Spread, inequality and clustering measures for the area’s private pools. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = -0.25. 0 hot-spot and 0 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of private pools density (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 10 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over private pools density: **High-High** = a dense neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a sparse one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

Private pools density per km² for each administrative sub-area, ordered from highest to lowest.

artifacts.name: Provision vs population
artifacts.summary: Do private pools track where people live? Private pools per 1,000 inhabitants against each sub-area’s population. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is an administrative sub-area, plotting its population against its private pools per 1,000 inhabitants. Sub-areas low on the vertical axis but high on the horizontal axis are under-served relative to their residents — an equity signal a density map cannot show.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision per capita
artifacts.summary: Private pools per 1,000 residents across the sub-areas — provision relative to need. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by its number of private pools per 1,000 inhabitants, so the colour reflects provision *relative to residents* rather than raw density. A populous sub-area with average density can still read as under-served here. Sub-areas without usable population data are omitted.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Coverage on foot
artifacts.summary: About 29% of the area is within 300 m on foot of a private pool. About 29% of residents are within reach. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The area of interest split into the part within reach (on foot) of any feature and the part beyond it. Reachability is computed using straight-line distance.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Underserved areas
artifacts.summary: Share of each neighbourhood beyond 300 m on foot of any private pool. About 42,859 residents live beyond that reach. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by the fraction of its area that lies **beyond reach** (on foot) of any feature — the complement of the coverage map. Darker = more underserved. Use it to target where new provision would reach the most currently-unserved people.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Most underserved sub-areas

artifacts.description:

artifacts.name: Private pools heatmap
artifacts.summary: A gridded density of private pools across the area — brighter means more. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area of interest, each cell shaded by how many private pools fall within it. It reveals clusters and gaps that individual points can hide.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Private pools density surface
artifacts.summary: A smoothed, continuous density surface of private pools (kernel-style). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A kernel-smoothed density of private pools: the point counts are blurred into a continuous surface so clusters show as smooth hot regions rather than individual grid cells — a boundary-free complement to the sub-area choropleth and the raw heatmap.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Distance to nearest private pool
artifacts.summary: How far to the nearest private pool from anywhere in the area (metres). Darker = further. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area, each cell shaded by the straight-line distance to the nearest private pool. Dark cells are the furthest from any feature — the access gaps. Straight-line (not routed), so it is an optimistic lower bound; it needs no routing service.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Data currentness
artifacts.summary: How recently each private pool was last edited in OpenStreetMap (median 3 yr ago). Darker = longer since the last edit. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is a feature, shaded by the number of years since its last OpenStreetMap edit (measured against the data snapshot). Clusters of dark points mark areas where the OSM picture is ageing and may warrant a re-survey — a spatial companion to the data-quality note.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: private_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.
